# Job Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 418r–418v

---

**6:1** And-answered Iyyov and-said:

**6:2** "If only weighing [shaqol] were-weighed [yishaqel] my-vexation [ka'asiy],
and-my-calamity [havvatiy] in-the-balances [be-moznayim] together they-would-lift [yis'u].

**6:3** For now more-than-the-sand of-the-seas [me-chol yammim] it-would-be-heavy [yikhbad];
therefore my-words [devaray] have-been-rash [la'u].

**6:4** For the-arrows [chitssei] of-Shaddai [the Almighty] [are] with-me [immadiy],
whose poison [chamatam] my-spirit [ruchiy] drinks [shotah];
the-terrors [bi'utei] of-God [eloah] are-arrayed [ya'arkhu] against-me.

**6:5** Does-the-wild-donkey [pere] bray [yinhaq] over [alei] grass [deshe]?
Or lows [yig'eh] the-ox [shor] over [al] his-fodder [belilo]?

**6:6** Can-that-which-is-tasteless [tafal] be-eaten [ye'akhel] without salt [mi-beli melach]?
Or is-there taste [ta'am] in-the-juice of-purslane [be-rir challamut]?

**6:7** My-soul [nafshiy] refuses [me'anah] to-touch [li-ngo'a];
they [are] like-the-sickness [ki-devei] of-my-bread [lachmiy].

**6:8** Who will-grant [mi yitten] that-comes [tavo] my-request [she'elatiy],
and-my-hope [tiqvatiy] God [eloah] would-give [yitten]?

**6:9** And-would-be-willing [ve-yo'el] God [eloah] to-crush-me [viyedakke'eniy],
would-let-loose [yatter] his-hand and-cut-me-off [vivyatse'eniy]!

**6:10** And-it-would-still-be [u-tehiy od] my-comfort [nechamatiy],
and-I-would-exult [va-asalledah] in-pain [be-chilah] without-mercy [lo yachmol]:
for I-have-not denied [lo kichadtiy] the-words [imrei] of-the-Holy-One [qadosh].

**6:11** What [is] my-strength [kochiy] that I-should-wait [ayachel]?
And-what [is] my-end [qitsiy] that I-should-prolong [a'arikh] my-soul [nafshiy]?

**6:12** Is my-strength the-strength of-stones [even]?
Or [is] my-flesh [besariy] bronze [nechusah]?

**6:13** Is-there-not [ha-lo] no-help [ein ezratiy] in-me,
and-success [tushiyyah] is-driven [niddechah] from-me?

**6:14** To-the-despairing [la-mas] from-his-friend [me-re'ehu] — kindness [chesed],
or the-fear of-Shaddai [the Almighty] he-forsakes [ya'azov].

**6:15** My-brothers [achay] have-dealt-treacherously [bagdu] like-a-wadi [ke-nachal],
like-the-channel [ke-afiq] of-wadis [nechalim] that-pass-away [ya'avoru].

**6:16** That are-dark [ha-qoderim] from [minei] ice [qerach],
upon-them hides [yit'allem] snow [shaleg].

**6:17** At-the-time [be-et] they-are-scorched [yezorbu] they-are-silenced [nitshmatu];
when-it-is-hot [be-chummo] they-are-extinguished [nid'akhu] from-their-place [mi-meqomam].

**6:18** The-paths [orchot] of-their-way [darkam] turn-aside [yillafetu];
they-go-up into-the-waste [tohu] and-perish [yovedu].

**6:19** The-caravans [orchot] of-Tema looked [hibbitu];
the-travelers [halikot] of-Sheva hoped [qivvu] for-them.

**6:20** They-were-ashamed [boshu] because he-trusted [batach];
they-came [ba'u] to-it and-were-confounded [vayechparu].

**6:21** For now you-have-become [heyitem] nothing [lo];
you-see [tir'u] terror [chatath] and-you-fear [vattiira'u].

**6:22** Did I say [he-amarti], 'Give [havu] to-me'?
Or 'From-your-wealth [kochakhem] offer-a-bribe [shichdu] for-me'?

**6:23** Or 'Deliver-me [malletuniy] from-the-hand of-the-enemy [tsar]'?
Or 'From-the-hand of-the-ruthless [aritsim] redeem-me [tifdduniy]'?

**6:24** Teach-me [horuniy] and-I will-be-silent [acharish],
and-what I-have-erred [shagitiy] make-me-understand [havinu liy].

**6:25** How-forceful [ma nimretsu] are-words [imrei] of-uprightness [yosher]!
But what [mah] does-reproving [yokiyach] from-you [mikkem] reprove [hokhiach]?

**6:26** Do-you-think to-reprove [le-hokhi'ach] words [millim]?
And-for-the-wind [ve-le-ruach] the-speeches [imrei] of-the-despairing [no'ash]?

**6:27** Even upon the-orphan [yatom] you-would-cast-lots [tappilu],
and-you-would-bargain [tikhru] over your-friend [re'ekhem].

**6:28** And-now be-willing [ho'ilu] — turn [penu] to-me [biy],
and-to your-face [al peneikhem] surely I-will-not lie [im akazzev].

**6:29** Turn [shuvu] now — let-there-be-no injustice [avlah];
turn [shuvu] — still my-righteousness [tsidqatiy] is-in-it.

**6:30** Is-there injustice [avlah] on-my-tongue [bi-leshoniy]?
Cannot my-palate [chikkiy] discern [lo yavin] calamity [havvot]?"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — "arrows of Shaddai":** Iyyov attributes his suffering directly to God — not the Adversary, not chance. The *chitssei Shaddai* (arrows of the Almighty) whose poison his spirit drinks is one of the most vivid images of divine assault in the Hebrew Bible.

**v.15-20 — The wadi metaphor:** This extended comparison of faithless friends to seasonal wadis (*nachal*) is drawn from desert geography. In winter, wadis run full with water from ice and snow; in summer when travelers are parched, they are bone-dry. The friends promise much and deliver nothing.

**v.6 — "juice of purslane":** The Hebrew *chalamut* is of uncertain identification — perhaps purslane, mallow, or egg-white. The point is clear: Elifaz's theology is as tasteless and insipid as flavorless food.

---
*— EMET*
